newsitem.title: UK: UK shares end weaker after UK data, Dow sell-off.
newsitem.headline: UK shares end weaker after UK data, Dow sell-off.

text.p: ** FTSE 100 retreats further from record levels, hit by
weak Dow and unexpectedly strong UK economic data.
** Dow succumbs to profit-taking, down 21 points at close.
** Smiths Industries results lift shares, prompt upgrades.
** GEC falls, BAe gains on Thomson SA privatisation news.
Many investors remained sidelined ahead of U.S. CPI numbers later in the day, which brought signs of relief by coming in on target to show a 0.3 percent rise.
But Wall Street was unexcited by the news and succumed to another bout of profit-taking, taking London with it. As markets here closed the Dow had lost 21-points.

Today's UK economic figures brought home the realisation that interest rates would have to go up, said Andy Hartwill, strategist at SocGen. "This market is being driven by the perpetual hope that interest rate increases are something you read about in fairy stories," he said.

September unemployment fell 35,600 against forecasts of a 20,000 fall. A PSBR of 3.41 billion stg compared with expectations of 2.7 billion stg and August average earnings rose 4.0 pct, versus the 3.75 pct forecast. All provided signs of economic acceleration, strategists said.
The December long gilt future tumbled through key support levels to settle at 109-22/32, down 1-3/32 on the day.
"The figures were disappointing for the bulls," Hartwill said. "But the economy can't be the best in Europe and be immune from falling unemployment," he added.
Hartwill has a year-end FTSE target of 3,850.
Activity amongst individual stocks was patchy, said dealers, and selling remained sporadic. Losers outweighed gainers by roughly four-to-one.
"We are seeing some profit-taking in the sectors that have been doing very well lately," said one dealer. "Banks, oils and pharmaceuticals."
"Banks are seeing continuing strong loan demand but if interest rates go up the sector will be ripe for profit-taking."
Elsewhere, British Aerospace was a gainer and GEC among the losers, after news that Lagardere was the French government's preferred bidder for the privatisation of Thomson SA.
BAe finished up 18p at 11.31-1/2 stg and GEC closed
Satellite broadcaster BSkyB fell 12p to 664-1/2p after cautious comments from BZW stalled its recent rally.
Shares in EMI ended down 17-1/2p at 12.77-1/2 stg on a downbeat comment in the Financial Times today. nL16198171
But Smiths Industries added 13p to 804-1/2p after full-year results came in at the top end of forecasts. nL16109076
Tate & Lyle lost 13p to 483-1/2p, hit by worries over a U.S. federal investigation into price fixing in the corn sweeteners market. nL16287248
